questions.question:
Write a poetry analysis response, analysing the poem “The Poison Tree” by William Blake
HINTS:
1. Subject:
Anger that is concealed rather than spoken, and what it becomes.
(The first stanza sets out the whole argument in four lines. Everything after it demonstrates the second half of that opening contrast.)
2. Most prominent poetic devices:
  • Extended metaphor — the wrath is treated as a plant throughout: watered, sunned, grown, and eventually bearing fruit. The metaphor is never explained and never dropped.
  • Contrast — the friend takes two lines, and the wrath ends; the foe takes fourteen, and the wrath kills. The imbalance is itself the argument.
  • Symbolism — the apple in a garden, taken in secret at night, carries an association the reader recognises before Blake does anything with it.
3. Theme(s):
Suppressed anger does not fade; it is actively cultivated, and concealment is the work that feeds it.
Word Limit: 200-250
